result.topic_en: An independent iterative computation (via tangents and half-sums of angles, related to the arithmetic-geometric mean) of the integral of sqrt(a^2 sin^2 T + b^2 cos^2 T) dT, i.e. elliptic arc length.
result.transcription:
Eine independente Rechnung ist folgende
$\frac{a}{b}\,\mathrm{tg}\,T = \mathrm{tg}\,U$
$\mathrm{tg}\,T' = \sqrt{\mathrm{tg}\,T . \mathrm{tg}\,U}\;,\quad U' = \frac{1}{2}(T+U)$
$\mathrm{tg}\,2T'' = \sqrt{\mathrm{tg}\,2T'\,\mathrm{tg}\,2U'},\quad U'' = \frac{1}{2}(T'+U')$
$\mathrm{tg}\,4T''' = \sqrt{\mathrm{tg}\,4T''\,\mathrm{tg}\,4U''}\;\; U''' = \frac{1}{2}(T''+U'')$
u.s.w.
dann ist $T^{\infty} = U^{\infty} = \theta$

$\int \sqrt{(aa\sin T^2 + bb\cos T^2)}\, dT$
$= \frac{\theta}{\mu}\left(a'a' - 2(a''a''-b''b'') - 4(a'''a'''-b'''b''')\ldots\right)$
$+\frac{1}{2}(a-b)\sin 2U' - \frac{1}{2}(a'-b')\sin 4U''$
$- \frac{1}{2}(a''-b'')\sin 8U''' - \frac{1}{2}(a'''-b''')\sin 16U^{IV}$

methods.what: Iterative angle transformation (tangent geometric mean and angle half-sum) converging to a common limit theta, analogous to the arithmetic-geometric mean
Limit of the iteration: both angle sequences converge to the same value theta
Series expression for the incomplete elliptic integral of the second kind (elliptic arc length) in terms of AGM sequences a^(n), b^(n), M = mu, and the iterated angles

items.english: The integral of sqrt(a^2 sin^2 T + b^2 cos^2 T) dT equals theta/mu times (a'a' - 2(a''a''-b''b'') - 4(a'''a'''-b'''b''') ...) plus a series of sine terms.
